concurrency_primitives: sync.WaitGroup + 2 goroutines (main.go:142-152), one per CSV; no channels, no worker pool
design_patterns: None realized; streaming per-file summarize() helper, single main.go
questions: Which 311 service-request types appear most often?
Which neighborhoods have the most 311 requests?
Which offenses or charge descriptions appear most often in arrest records?
Which neighborhoods or districts appear most often in arrest records?
Which matching area labels have records in both datasets? (combined counts; exploratory)
overview: Terse single-file Go program: two goroutines each stream one CSV into type/area count maps, then five top-8 ASCII bar charts are printed. Code is tidy and race-free with two small tests, but there is no package structure, no realized design pattern, and the only cross-dataset step is a case-sensitive label intersection.
stakeholder_value: No stakeholders are named and four of five questions are single-dataset frequency counts. The one join sums 311 and arrest counts per matching label, which the README itself calls exploratory and non-interpretable; on real data it matches a single label ('CARE') due to case mismatch. A city office would gain no actionable insight.
issues: Sample CSVs are fabricated (headers crime_type/service_type do not match Open Baltimore); real data absent with no URL or fetch script
Cross-dataset join (main.go:170-175) is case-sensitive and collapses to one match on real data
Token concurrency: two goroutines, no pool, sequential join/aggregate
Per-row map allocation and silent skipping of malformed rows
README gives Windows instructions first and no dataset links; only --offline path runs
rationale: Full build credit and partial memory credit for a clean, streaming, race-free build. Heavy deductions for fabricated sample-only data, token concurrency, single-dataset questions with a broken join, and a default run path that exits with an error because required data is neither bundled nor fetchable. 48/100 = F.
